text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Attackers launch 80 Molotov cocktails at Basque police patrol on Sunday.
- Brussels to examine Telefonica purchase of Antena 3 Television.
- Treasury demands CELSA pay 10 billion pesetas for alleged tax offence.
EL MUNDO
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and leader of United Left coalition Julio Anguita meet and come closer on ideas on how to combate violence by Basque separatist group ETA.
- High Court judge Baltasar Garzon accepts call by managing director of Sogecable Juan Luis Cebrian to investigate fellow judge Javier Gomez de Liano who ran case on Sogecable.
- European industry asks Catalan president Jordi Pujol that they not be obliged to print labels in Catalan.
DIARIO 16
- Garzon to investigate Liano.
ABC
- Aznar says in Bilbao: "There is little to negotiate with those who are dedicated to violence".
CINCO DIAS
- New lottery shops to be introduced into hypermarkets.
- Spanish stock market is rising, but still third worst performer in Europe this year.
- Number of mobile phones contracted in first half slightly above one million, but those who actually use service only reached 450,000.
EXPANSION
- Seventy percent of fairground group Parque de Atracciones to be launched on stock market for 14 billion pesetas.
- Argentaria chairman assures that hostile takeover of his bank would be "unthinkable".
- Luis Marti Mingarro, dean of Madrid lawyers, asks government to ban auditors and lawyers from working together.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Argentaria chairman insists on independence of group and hopes for improvement in results of 10 percent.
- Jose Cosmen has decided to retire and passed Alsa group into hands of his son.
- Privatisation of Inespal will cost state 10 billion pesetas.
